architecture.title: From a GGUF on Hugging Face to an OpenAI API on the Spark
architecture.caption: You build llama.cpp on the Spark with CUDA for sm_121 (121a-real). llama-server -hf downloads the GGUF into ~/.cache/huggingface/hub and serves /v1/chat/completions and /health on port 30080 (the playbook uses 30000, which SGLang needs). LM Studio's headless llmster serves its own models on 1234. Both speak the same OpenAI API as Ollama, so the laptop's client code does not change.

sequence.title: Lab 04-2 — proving a GGUF's size from its header
sequence.caption: The lab reads only the header: magic, version, metadata (tokenizer included), then one entry per tensor with its shape and GGML type. Multiplying each shape by its type's bytes-per-block and adding it all up reproduced the gemma3:4b file on this Mac to within 27 bytes of alignment padding.
